1.why: Source P1: climb continues to a third ledge with a bolted anchor; stored notes also say third ledge
1.text: Stand on the third ledge, reached by the short chimney above the second large ledge.

2.why: Source P2 ends at a belay ledge with bolts; twin cracks and loose blocks are not in the source
2.text: Stand on a ledge with bolts at the top of the double crack pitch.

3.why: Source P3: finish on a nice belay ledge; 'directly above the offwidth/squeeze' is not stated
3.text: Stand on a good ledge at the top of the crux offwidth pitch.

4.why: Source P4: large ledge with a bolted belay; 'just below summit' conflicts with another source (60 ft of climbing above)
4.text: Stand on a large ledge at a bolted anchor, at the top of the face pitch.

P1.why: MP P1: follow triple crack to the end of the roof and belay; 'lip' came from P4 text
P1.text: Stand at the end of the roof where the triple crack system finishes.

P2.why: MP P2: belay from the big sandy ledge after the left-facing layback corner
P2.text: Stand on the big sandy ledge at the top of the layback corner.

P3.why: MP P3: belay on another large ledge above the twin handcrack; 'second' not stated
P3.text: Stand on a large ledge above the twin handcrack.

P4.why: Source's P4 belay is an ambiguous ledge anchor extended back to the lip, and wording closely follows the source; not a clear location

2.why: MP P2: continue up the featured face to a belay on the crest
2.text: Stand on the crest at the top of the featured face.

5.why: MP P5: climb the dihedral and exit up and right to an airy belay
5.text: Stand at an exposed stance just up and right of where the dihedral ends.

P1.why: MP P1: when the corner slabs out continue straight up, belay below the treed ledge
P1.text: Stand below the treed ledge, after the corner slabs out and you continue straight up.

P2.why: MP P2: belay on a second treed ledge; a tree is not stated by the source
P2.text: Stand on the second treed ledge above the tight, flaring corner.

P3.why: MP P3: step right just before the dihedral, belay on a mossy ledge
P3.text: Stand on a mossy ledge just right of the base of the left-facing dihedral.

P4.why: MP P4: layback at top of the tips corner to a ledge with a large snag; tree not stated by source
P4.text: Stand on the ledge with a large snag, at the top of the tips crack.
